 LIVE  Updated  now Scott Murray Sat 7 Nov 2026 09.24 EST First published on Sat 7 Nov 2026 06.00 EST Share Key events 11m ago GOAL! Leeds United 1-0 Tottenham Hotspur (Okafor 79) 
 1h ago HALF TIME: Leeds United 0-0 Tottenham Hotspur 
 3h ago The teams 
 3h ago Preamble 
 Noah Okafor whips off his shirt after scoring to give Leeds the advantage over Tottenham. Photograph: Oli Scarff/AFP/Getty Images View image in fullscreen Noah Okafor whips off his shirt after scoring to give Leeds the advantage over Tottenham. Photograph: Oli Scarff/AFP/Getty Images Scott Murray Sat 7 Nov 2026 09.24 EST First published on Sat 7 Nov 2026 06.00 EST Share Key events 11m ago GOAL! Leeds United 1-0 Tottenham Hotspur (Okafor 79) 
 1h ago HALF TIME: Leeds United 0-0 Tottenham Hotspur 
 3h ago The teams 
 3h ago Preamble 
 now 09.24 EST 90 min +2: Tonali dribbles down the left and finds Williams-Barnett in the box with a low cross. Williams-Barnett tries to sort his feet out for a shot, but can’t manage it. Leeds clear again.
 Share 17s ago 09.23 EST 90 min +1: Robertson swings a free kick in from the left. Van Hecke rises highest, and guides a header towards the top right. Trafford extends fully and tips around the post. The resulting corner leads to a throw, which is flung in illegally by Kulusevski. Pressure off!
 Share 2m ago 09.22 EST 90 min: There will be four additional minutes.
 Share 2m ago 09.21 EST 89 min: Wilson steps across Tonali, who swings an arm to bring him down and picks up a booking.
 Share 3m ago 09.20 EST 88 min: Meanwhile, Leeds are doing a marvellous job of containing Spurs, who are trying to respond, but can’t get anywhere near their opponents’ box. Leeds’ xG is now exactly 2 to Tottenham’s 0.28.
 Share 5m ago 09.19 EST 87 min: No, is the answer to that. Not a single one.
 Share 5m ago 09.18 EST 86 min: TNT are interviewing Nmecha as the game goes on, a box popping up and invading the action. Did any football fan ask for this sort of thing?
 Share 7m ago 09.16 EST 84 min: Kudus makes way for the 18-year-old Williams-Barnett. When the game restarts, Calvert-Lewin once again tears clear down the right, but doesn’t back himself to shoot, turning around instead and laying off to Okafor. The move breaks down. That’s a couple of big chances butchered by Calvert-Lewin today.
 Share 9m ago 09.14 EST 82 min: Spurs haven’t won any of their last 49 matches in which they’ve gone behind. No wonder Roberto De Zerbi looks thoroughly miserable. That goal was no more than Leeds deserved; they’ve been by far the better team in this second half.
 Share 11m ago 09.13 EST 80 min: VAR has a look at a possible handball by Wilson, but there was no touch with his arm. The goal stands!
 Share 11m ago 09.12 EST GOAL! Leeds United 1-0 Tottenham Hotspur (Okafor 79)
 Bard throws in from the left. Wilson swivels just inside the box, chesting down and teeing up Okafor, who takes a touch infield before lashing a shot across Kinsky and into the bottom left! Lovely move, and what a substitution!
 View image in fullscreen Substitute Noah Okafor breaks the deadlock! Photograph: Robbie Jay Barratt/AMA/Getty Images View image in fullscreen Photograph: Scott Heppell/Reuters Share Updated at  09.22 EST 14m ago 09.10 EST 77 min: Kinsky annoys Longstaff again by pawing his corner clear. Then Leeds make a double change, sending on Wilson and Okafor for Tanaka and Nmecha.
 Share 15m ago 09.09 EST 76 min: … but Spurs don’t clear their lines particularly well, and Tanaka strides down the left to win another Leeds corner. Longstaff, who must be wondering how he didn’t score, to take.
 Share 16m ago 09.08 EST 75 min: Bogle advances down the right and crosses low for Longstaff, who turns and launches a rising shot goalwards from 12 yards. It’s a superb effort, and heading in, but met by the fingertips of Kinsky. What a save! The ball clears the bar, and nothing comes of the corner.
 Share 18m ago 09.05 EST 73 min: Kulusevski and Bentancur combine down the right, but at such slow speed that Leeds close down all avenues to their box. Spurs have not created very much this afternoon.
 Share 20m ago 09.03 EST 71 min: From the set piece, Bogle shoots. The ball hits Bentancur. Leeds claim a penalty, but that’s hit Bentancur on the chest. No sir!
 Share 21m ago 09.02 EST 70 min: Bard loops down the middle. Nmecha tries to loop over Kinsky, who tips onto the bar. But he was offside. Then Calvert-Lewin fails to hit the target. But Kinsky takes his sweet time over the restart, so the referee awards a corner to Leeds!
 Share 23m ago 09.01 EST 68 min: Spurs play some possession stuff. They don’t really go anywhere for a while, but suddenly spring into action, Gallagher bringing the ball down on the edge of the Leeds D before pearling a low drive inches wide of the bottom left. Not entirely sure Trafford was getting to that. Spurs fans thought that was in, so are jeered for their cheer not long after.
 Share 25m ago 08.58 EST 66 min: … so Spurs make a triple change, replacing the ineffective Marmoush and Fernandes, plus Porro, who is on one-and-a-half yellows, with Kulusevski, Bentancur and Gallagher. Gray will take over from Porro at right-back.
 Share 27m ago 08.57 EST 64 min: Leeds have had seven attempts on goal during this second half. Spurs are yet to generate a single one.
 Share 28m ago 08.55 EST 63 min: Calvert-Lewin, Bard and Longstaff combine well down the left. The ball’s rolled infield for Ampadu, who shoots from 25 yards. The ball takes a huge deflection to the left, and had it stayed on target, it was a goal, because Kinsky had committed to diving the other way. But it squeaks out for a corner, which Kinsky claims. Leeds are getting closer and closer.
 Share 30m ago 08.54 EST 62 min: Van de Ven again over-eggs his dribble out from the back. This time he loses the ball, allowing Nmecha to enter the box from the left and aim a curler towards the top right. It’s not a good effort, and easily blocked.
 Share 31m ago 08.53 EST 61 min: Leeds are romping ahead in the xG stakes. It’s 1.11 to 0.22.
 Share 31m ago 08.52 EST 60 min: Porro clips Bard, who was advancing down the left, from behind. It should be a yellow. It’s not, though, presumably because it would have been a second yellow for Porro, and you know how referees process that sort of situation. Porro is now in the last-chance saloon. Meanwhile nothing comes of the resulting free kick.
 Share 33m ago 08.50 EST 58 min: The pace doesn’t drop, but passes are no longer sticking. All a bit messy for now.
 Share 35m ago 08.48 EST 56 min: Van de Ven over-elaborates when dribbling out from the back, and is nearly stripped by Longstaff. Had the Leeds man completed the challenge, he was through on goal. Van de Ven breathes out.
 Share 36m ago 08.47 EST 55 min: Tonali, dropping deep, tries to release Kudus down the right but has to settle for a corner. Kudus ambles across to take it. He exchanges passes with Solanke, then Robertson finally crosses long. Leeds deal with it. A bit of a waste.
 Share 38m ago 08.46 EST 53 min: Calvert-Lewin romps into space down the inside-right channel, chasing a fine Longstaff pass. He should shoot upon reaching the area, but lays off to Tanaka instead, who leans back and skies over the bar. Huge chance spurned.
 Share 39m ago 08.45 EST 52 min: Porro slides in, over the ball, and catches Nmecha on the shin. It’s a yellow. It should be a yellow. But Bogle’s far worse action in the first half should have been that at the very least . Roberto De Zerbi highlights this inherent contradiction, and is also booked for his trouble. Consistency? Good luck in your search for that.
 Share 41m ago 08.42 EST 50 min: Bogle crosses from the right. Calvert-Lewin prepares to sidefoot home from six yards, only for Van de Ven to nip in ahead of him, and slice the ball over his own bar and wide left. Then from the corner, hit long by Longstaff, Calvert-Lewin heads goalwards. Solanke blocks on his own line, then Elvedi heads wide left from close range. It should be 1-0.
 View image in fullscreen Close for Leeds! Photograph: Ryan Browne/Shutterstock Share Updated at  08.58 EST 43m ago 08.40 EST 48 min: Ampadu throws long from the right. Van de Ven clears. Leeds have had no joy with their long-throw weapon so far.
 Share 45m ago 08.38 EST 46 min: Bard’s very first act is to whip in a glorious low cross from his position on the left. Calvert-Lewin is on his heels and can’t connect. That was begging to be rammed home.
 Share 46m ago 08.37 EST Leeds get the second half started. They’ve replaced Gudmundsson with Bard.
 Share 54m ago 08.29 EST Half-time postbag. “Both feet are off the ground. That’s Bogle’s entire weight on Tel’s Achilles. That can lead to a serious injury. Bizarre decision” – Martin Perring
 “Why do red cards exist if not precisely to protect players?” – John from Norway
 “The most insane thing about VAR, and there are so many insane things about it, is that we have to watch replays of a player OBVIOUSLY doing a red-card challenge one thousand times in slow-motion, and it ends with not even a yellow. The chicken-shit nature of it all, the incompetence, all elevated because of technology. I hate it so, so much” – Øivind Idsø
 “There’s overthinking it, as you say, but this is like they’ve been given a task to find a reason for not giving that as a red, rocking and rolling desperately, frame-by-frame. The explanation they release for not giving a red should be a corker. Meanwhile, whatever happened to ‘clear and obvious’? VAR is almost single-handedly turning me into a grumpy old man. I’ll be off out now to shout at some pigeons” – Rob Knap
 “I’ve supported VAR from the start. It was always going to have teething issues as it was implemented, and it was never going to 100% eliminate mistakes. Subjectivity is still a thing. But, my word, they don’t half make it hard to defend at times. It should be established now, a mature technology with most of the errors ironed out. If anything, though, It’s getting worse. I’m not in the ‘Bin it’ camp yet, but I’m a lot closer than I was at the start of the season” – Matt Dony
 “Committees are an extremely useful method for decision making, especially when people have time to deliberate. But perhaps football refereeing isn’t suited to committees” – Kári Tulinius
 “That would have been a red card at Elland Road in the 70s ” – Gary Naylor
 Share 1h ago 08.22 EST HALF TIME: Leeds United 0-0 Tottenham Hotspur
 Leeds should have had a penalty; they should also have had a man sent off. The players walk down the tunnel. The referee was planning to drive away in his car, but the doors and square wheels have fallen off and there’s all smoke coming out of the radiator.
 Share 1h ago 08.21 EST 45 min +5: Ampadu throws long from the left. Van Hecke powers a header miles clear. Ampadu has another go. Van Hecke batters clear again. The xG does not change.
 Share 1h ago 08.20 EST 45 min +4: The xG, for what that’s worth, is 0.19 to 0.22. Meanwhile Roberto De Zerbi continues to give the fourth official the what-for. His post-match interview could make for good entertainment.
 Share 1h ago 08.18 EST 45 min +2: Fernandes slices a low drive miles off target. After nearly boiling over, this half is now fizzling out, which is probably for the best all round.
 Share 1h ago 08.17 EST 45 min: There will be six minutes of additional first-half time, most of which a result of the on-field referee and VAR spending ages failing to make a decision.
 Share 1h ago 08.15 EST 44 min: Kudus fizzes a tempting low cross through the Leeds six-yard box from the right. What a ball. But neither Gray nor Solanke respond. Any touch and it was the opening goal.
 Share 1h ago 08.14 EST 43 min: Tel limps off. A heavy trudge, he’s in some difficulty. He’s replaced by Solanke.
 Share 1h ago 08.13 EST 42 min: Marmoush clips Muharemovic from behind. That should be a booking as well, but the referee has lost control of this with his unwillingness to make any sort of decision whatsoever. Meanwhile Tel goes down, he looks really unhappy.
 Share 1h ago 08.11 EST 40 min: Tel is getting dog’s abuse now. He’s also moving very gingerly, having recently had someone stand on his ankle.
 Share 1h ago 08.11 EST 39 min: Roberto De Zerbi isn’t happy about that. You can’t blame him. Meanwhile the game restarts, with Bogle, who shouldn’t be on the pitch, crossing for Nmencha, who plants a header straight at Kinsky. Had that gone in, there would have been some wild scenes all right.
 Share 1h ago 08.09 EST 38 min: No red card, no serious foul play. That is preposterous enough in itself; that there’s not even a yellow is beyond a joke. The on-field referee should have seen that, at the very least.
 Share 1h ago 08.07 EST 37 min: VAR is flapping taking a long time over this. You can overthink these things, you know.
 Share 1h ago 08.06 EST 36 min: It’s a really poor challenge, studs landing on Tel’s achilles, the Spurs player’s leg bending. It should be a red card.
 Share 1h ago 08.06 EST 35 min: VAR is in fact checking for a red card. The on-field referee, it should be noted, has completely abdicated responsibility.
 Share 1h ago 08.05 EST 34 min: Bogle leaves one on Tel, who was in the process of spinning him. It’s a really poor challenge, studs on ankle. A red card wouldn’t be out of the question here; there’s not even a yellow shown.
 View image in fullscreen Mathys Tel recieves treatment after the challenge from Jayden Bogle. Photograph: Annabel Lee-Ellis/PA Share Updated at  08.17 EST 1h ago 08.04 EST 33 min: A long pass down the left confuses Elvedi into conceding a corner with a misjudged backwards header. One corner leads to another, then Marmoush heads harmlessly wide. To be fair, Trafford has had next to nothing to do as well, if you ignore a couple of long-range shots scuffed straight at him.
